articles.title: Escitalopram reduces anger and irritability in premenstrual dysphoric disorder, study finds
articles.summary: New research shows that administering the antidepressant escitalopram during the luteal phase eases the debilitating irritability and anger associated with premenstrual dysphoric disorder, while simultaneously reducing the brain’s neural response to aggressive social stimuli.

articles.title: Study of 1.9 million people finds a striking link between ADHD and gut problems
articles.summary: Researchers analyzing data from more than 1.9 million people found that ADHD is associated with substantially higher rates of digestive problems. People with ADHD had nearly double the odds of constipation, 58% higher odds of irritable bowel syndrome, and more than four times the odds of encopresis.

articles.title: How a parent’s motivation influences their child’s writing skills
articles.summary: When parents help their children with writing activities because they genuinely enjoy the process, children develop more positive attitudes toward the subject. These positive feelings are linked to better handwritten stories and improved grammar in the classroom.

articles.title: Halo: Improving forecast accuracy through heteroscedastic estimation
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.10589v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Heteroscedastic forecasting, where a network estimates a scale parameter alongside a location parameter, is normally motivated by uncertainty quantification. This paper shows it also improves the point estimate, in contrast to reported negative results for heteroscedastic estimation outside time series. Halo is a modification that reuses an existing deep forecaster's architecture, giving it a second output for the scale of its implied distribution and training it under the matching negative log likelihood. articles.title: Byzantine-Robust Federated Fire Detection with a Rotating Coordinator
articles.summary: arXiv:2609.10647v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the application of federated learning (FL) to indoor fire detection. Existing federated solutions leave three practical obstacles unaddressed: limited uplink bandwidth, Byzantine (malicious or faulty) clients, and unconditional trust in a single, permanently fixed aggregation server. articles.summary: arXiv:2609.10566v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The pulling illusion induced by asymmetric vibration stimuli has attracted attention for its potential applications in rehabilitation and sensory assessment. articles.summary: arXiv:2609.10947v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We propose the Platonic brain bridge hypothesis: omni models, which process video, audio and text jointly like the brain, converge on brain-like representations, and the correspondence is bidirectional. articles.title: Semaglutide may protect against psychiatric disorders independent of weight loss
articles.summary: New research suggests that higher doses of the weight-loss drug semaglutide might lower the risk of developing certain mental health conditions. Surprisingly, this psychiatric benefit appears to be independent of how much weight a person actually loses.

articles.title: Brain scans reveal how recurrent depression leaves a lasting mark on the amygdala
articles.summary: A large study found that a history of multiple depressive episodes is tied to heightened brain activity during emotional processing. The findings suggest each episode leaves a biological signature, increasing vulnerability to future relapses.
